summary: Eight comment-endorsed finds spanning security tools, content management, media, VR and retro computing.
telegram_footer: 8 items surfaced | 30/30 past-front-page stories processed | history + run artifact updated

items.name: Aikido Safe Chain
items.source_story_title: Compromised LiteLLM 1.107.0 on PyPI Installs a Credential Stealer and Backdoor
items.summary: Package-manager wrapper that checks dependencies for malicious code before installation.
items.why_included: A first-hand user recommends a cross-package-manager safeguard in a supply-chain discussion.
items.evidence: sunbum says they use Safe Chain because package managers can be configured incorrectly.

evidence_sources.author: sunbum
evidence_sources.excerpt: I use safechain for this, because there is always gonna be another package manager configured wrong.

items.name: cargo-audit
items.source_story_title: Today's PHP security release, and how we're strengthening security
items.summary: Rust dependency auditor that checks Cargo lockfiles against known security advisories.
items.why_included: A working developer offers a concrete tool for keeping track of vulnerable dependencies.
items.evidence: berkes reports using cargo audit for Rust applications to check dependencies against CVEs.

evidence_sources.author: berkes
evidence_sources.excerpt: For my rust applications, I use "cargo audit" which checks all dependencies against the CVEs.

items.name: debsecan
items.source_story_title: Today's PHP security release, and how we're strengthening security
items.summary: Debian security analyzer that reports known vulnerabilities in installed packages.
items.why_included: A specific host-level auditing recommendation complements application dependency checks.
items.evidence: berkes recommends debsecan for reporting CVEs in installed software, describing an Ubuntu use case.

evidence_sources.author: berkes
evidence_sources.excerpt: For the rest of the stack `debsecan` does exactly what you want on Ubuntu: report CVEs for installed software.

items.name: Drupal
items.source_story_title: Drupal is now light-years ahead of its reputation
items.summary: Open-source CMS recommended for governed users, structured content and publishing workflows.
items.why_included: An independent comment gives a precise use-case recommendation rather than generic launch praise.
items.evidence: scottfalconer recommends Drupal when governed users, content and workflow require battle-tested defaults.

evidence_sources.author: scottfalconer
evidence_sources.excerpt: I'd recommend Drupal specifically when you have the need for strong governed management of users + content + workflow and you want something that is battle tested without having to make all the decisions that get you there.

items.name: Sean Carroll’s Mindscape
items.source_story_title: In Hilbert space, all things are quantumly possible
items.summary: Science-and-philosophy podcast; an HN listener particularly recommends the David Wallace episode.
items.why_included: A direct recommendation includes a concrete episode as an entry point.
items.evidence: librasteve calls Mindscape excellent and particularly likes its David Wallace episode.

evidence_sources.author: librasteve
evidence_sources.excerpt: Sean Carroll (name checked in the article) has an excellent podcast “Mindscape” (https://preposterousuniverse.com/podcast/) I particularly like the one with David Wallace.

items.name: Cogito’s West Papua documentary
items.source_story_title: Tiny possum and glider thought extinct for 6000 years found in remote West Papua
items.summary: West Papua history documentary praised for deep research and extensive citations.
items.why_included: An emphatic viewer recommendation supplies a direct video link and a clear research-quality rationale.
items.evidence: culi highly recommends Cogito's West Papua documentary and praises its research and citations.

evidence_sources.author: culi
evidence_sources.excerpt: Cogito, who does some of the most astounding and in-depth research on global histories, just came out with an incredible documentary about the history of West Papua that changed the way I see it forever. I highly recommend it (and most of Cogito's work. Even his extensive citations are worth spending time with)

items.name: Brass Tactics
items.source_story_title: Way to Play Super Mario 64: On Apple Vision Pro
items.summary: Oculus Rift real-time strategy game played across a living tabletop battlefield.
items.why_included: A former player identifies a distinctive VR favorite rather than merely mentioning a game.
items.evidence: bni calls Brass Tactics their favorite during regular Oculus use and praises its unique play style.

evidence_sources.author: bni
evidence_sources.excerpt: Back when I used my Oculus a lot, a RTS game called Brass Tactics was my favorite.
